title: City of Toronto M365 commitment case
decision_question: How much licence capacity should a buyer commit to before infrastructure and deployment readiness are certain?

published_facts.fact: The agreement covered 10,000 enterprise users and two add-ons, described by the audit as 30,000 subscription licences.
The published annual subscription cost for the initial commitment was $5,140,800.
At the end of the first agreement year, the audit reported 7.5% deployment and $4,755,240 of unused subscription cost.
For the first nine months of the second year, the audit reported 44.5% usage and $2,141,357 of unused subscription cost.

simulation_notice: Only the upfront cost proxy is derived from the public audit. The rollout distribution, delay probability, alternative price premiums, review frequencies, and true-down rights below are illustrative assumptions used to demonstrate the tool. They are not City of Toronto or Microsoft contract terms.

optimization_template.name: Negotiable policy template
optimization_template.description: A modelling template whose floor matches the audit's reported 7.5% Year 1 deployment. It is used to search hypothetical commitment, review, buffer, and true-down policies and is not a published Toronto or Microsoft offer.

commercial_options.name: Published upfront commitment proxy
commercial_options.description: A modelling proxy derived by dividing the published annual subscription cost by 30,000 subscription-equivalent units and 12 months.

commercial_options.name: Illustrative quarterly ramp
commercial_options.description: A hypothetical quarterly activation ramp priced at a 15% premium to the public cost proxy.

commercial_options.name: Illustrative monthly flexibility
commercial_options.description: A hypothetical monthly true-up/true-down construct priced at a 25% premium to the public cost proxy.
